html:
SMTO-BOOT-0035 — The model server didn't confirm the model the benchmark expected

GUID: a4fa54c1-f810-49b5-a1fd-5e44af07c518
Slug: boot-model-identity-mismatch
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The benchmark started a model server, but the server never confirmed it was serving the expected model. The benchmark stopped that server and skipped this model rather than test the wrong one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the newest benchmark-….md report in src/vllm/results/ and find this model's section. Look for “last_seen=” or “last_error=” near the end of the message. This shows whether the server listed no model yet, listed a different one, or stopped answering.
  2. If last_seen shows no model name, the model was probably still loading. Run the benchmark again for just this model and add --server-timeout 120. By default the benchmark waits only 30 seconds for the model's name to appear after the server first answers.
  3. If you see last_error, open this model's .server.log file in src/vllm/results/ and read the last lines to see why the server stopped answering. The server writes the reason it closed or failed in that log; the benchmark only sees that it went quiet.
  4. If a different model name is listed, run echo $MODEL_ID in the same terminal. If it prints a name, run unset MODEL_ID, then run the benchmark again. The start scripts load whatever model MODEL_ID names, which replaces the one this benchmark entry expects.

What success looks like

  • The benchmark runs its questions against that model and the report shows a score for it.

If it still fails

  • Send this model's section of the benchmark report and its .server.log file from src/vllm/results/ to the person who maintains your model setup. Don't point the benchmark at a different server to get past this; the score would then belong to the wrong model.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • After the launched profile's server first answered, wait_for_expected_server did not see the profile's model_id in /v1/models within --server-timeout (default 30 s), so the benchmark stopped the server and recorded a startup failure (the message carries last_seen or last_error).

What this means

  • Expected-model polling reaches its deadline without observing the required model ID in the endpoint's model list. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Expected-model polling reaches its deadline without observing the required model ID in the endpoint's model list.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect last seen model IDs and connection errors against the selected profile/base URL.

How to fix it

  • Read last_seen or last_error in that profile's section of benchmark-*.md. An empty last_seen means the server listed no models yet (rerun the profile with a larger --server-timeout); last_error means it stopped answering (read the profile's .server.log in src/vllm/results/). A server that lists only other model IDs normally keeps launch_profile waiting until --startup-timeout (SMTO-BOOT-0037); if last_seen names another model, unset an exported MODEL_ID that overrides the start script or fix the PROFILES model_id/script mismatch.
  • Inspect the served model ID and selected endpoint; stop or reconfigure only the intended server.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended endpoint reports the exact expected model identity.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
